newsitem.title: RUSSIA: 100 days into second term, Yeltsin said recovering.
newsitem.headline: 100 days into second term, Yeltsin said recovering.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin, who underwent heart surgery nearly two weeks ago, was said to be recovering well at the weekend as he marked 100 days into his second term in office.

Doctors said Yeltsin, who has scarcely been in the Kremlin since he was reelected on July 3, planned to leave the hospital where he has been recuperating for a walk on Sunday at the Barvikha sanatorium outside Moscow.

"This morning Boris Nikolayevich not only spoke to us, he got up, shoved all the doctors aside and said: "Look, boys, yesterday I worked and I can walk like this now," Renat Akchurin, the surgeon who led Yeltsin's operation, told a news briefing. Yeltsin then marched across the room, he added.
The head of the Kremlin medical centre, Sergei Mironov, said Yeltsin would start meeting officials next week and would hold talks with Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on Tuesday.

Chernomyrdin has been given greater powers during Yeltsin's illness, but the Kremlin leader's absence from the political scene has lead to fierce infighting within his entourage which flared again last week.
Yeltsin would move from the Central Clinical Hospital to Barvikha on Thursday or Friday, Mironov told the briefing for Russian news media.
"The president's recuperation is going well. The president is active, Today he is going for a walk at the dacha in Barvikha, to be in normal surroundings for a while,"

Akchurin, who led the November 5 quintuple bypass surgery on Yeltsin, said the 65-year-old president had lost weight but had got stronger since the operation, designed to allow him to return to normal life.

Akchurin said scarring on Yeltsin's heart revealed during the bypass surgery had backed up his earlier view that Yeltsin had suffered a third, unannounced heart attack shortly before the presidential run-off.
Reporters were kept away from the Central Clinical Hospital on Sunday and did not see the presidential cortege enter or leave the complex.
A Russian newspaper on Saturday published the first picture of Yeltsin since the operation to clear the blood supply problems which had led to the attacks.

The photograph, taking up much of the front page of the liberal daily Sevodnya, showed a relaxed-looking Yeltsin wearing an open-necked shirt and patterned cardigan drinking tea with his wife Naina and granddaugher Masha.
Sevodnya said the photograph, released by the presidential press service, was taken on Friday in the presidential wing of the hospital.
Later the press service said Yeltsin had worked four hours on Saturday on official papers, one hour longer than on Friday, and had signed a series of decrees.
The picture and reports seemed to be the latest step in the Kremlin's strategy of reassuring the country that Yeltsin was recovering fast and in control of affairs of state.
But some newspapers were sceptical at the weekend after a new scandal broke around his chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais.

"Who are the people at the helm of the country?" a headline in the communist opposition daily Sovietskaya Rossiya said after a fresh round of mudslinging between Chubais and Yeltsin's former bodyguard Alexander Korzhakov.

Saturday marked 100 days since Yeltsin was reelected, but because of his heart problems he has only been in the Kremlin a few times. Most of his time has been spent in Barvikha, a complex of government rest houses outside Moscow.

Kremlin press secretary Sergei Yastrzhembsky said on Friday a planned address to the nation, Yeltsin's first public act, was still being prepared, but he did not say when it would be. "You understand, the imagemakers want the president's appearance to have a big impact," he said.
Itar-Tass news agency quoted the doctors as saying on Sunday that the president was ready to address the nation at any time but it was up to him to decide the date.
